name: Uisai
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Laycock, Donald C. 2003. A Dictionary of Buin, a language of Bougainville (Uisai treated as Buin variety); also Allen & Hurd 1965 Bougainville survey. Neither reachable online to verify a stress statement.

sources.citation: Griffin, Margie. 1996. Buin Organised Phonology Data (Buin (Telei, Terei) Language [BUO]). 4 pp. ms., SIL PNG Branch, Ukarumpa. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 42446.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 3 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)': 'Stress is predictable. In two and three syllable words stress occurs on the first syllable. In four and five syllable words primary stress occurs on the second syllable. On long verbs there are layers of stress.' Header names the language as Buin [BUO] with no dialect; Uisai is never mentioned (only 'skin in some dialects' for katua). This is the Terei (tere1278) statement, not a Uisai one.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 2003. A dictionary of Buin, a language of Bougainville (ed. Masayuki Onishi). Pacific Linguistics 537. Canberra: ANU. xxvii+355 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Preface p. viii: 'Uisai, spoken in the northeastern part, is most distinct'; p. xi lists 'NE Northeastern (Uisai) dialect' among five dialects, data based on central Buin (Paariro). 'Elementary Buin grammar' sec. 1 Phonology pp. xiii-xiv: phoneme inventory, consonant sequences, allophony, syllabification, morphophonemics; nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the book (0 text-layer hits for stress/accent/prosody/intonation); the c. 249 NE (Uisai) dialect forms carry no accent marks.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1982. Melanesian linguistic diversity: a Melanesian choice? In R. J. May & Hank Nelson (eds), Melanesia: beyond diversity, vol. 1, 33-38. Canberra: Research School of Pacific Studies, ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 36: 'The clearest example is found in the Uisai dialect of Buin, in south Bougainville.. The Uisai dialect has about 1,000 speakers. In this dialect, we find all the gender agreements reversed'; only Uisai-specific published discussion found; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 1975. The East Papuan Phylum in general. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 783-804.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: pp. 791-794: Buin family census lists 'Uitai 1200' (= Uisai) as a Buin dialect; East Bougainville Stock has 'very simple segmental phonologies with small phoneme inventories'; Buin phoneme chart after Laycock, 'Syllable structure is simple'; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1969. Sublanguages in Buin: play, poetry, and preservation. Pacific Linguistics A-22 (Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 10): 1-23. DOI 10.15144/PL-A22.1
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: fn. 3 pp. 1-2 summarises (central) Buin phonology: phonemes, syllabification, reduplication types; silent on stress; Uisai not mentioned.

sources.citation: Griffin, Margie. 1974. Notes on the Buin language. 39 pp. manuscript, SIL (Glottolog ref 555474, grammar sketch).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only grammar sketch of Buin by the long-term SIL fieldworker; may restate the stress rule with dialect remarks, possibly covering the Uisai (NE) dialect.

sources.citation: Onahas, Jack. 2002. Torikale pailehi. Wycliffe Bible Translators, 40 pp; and Uisai primer 1. 1986. Arawa: Dept of North Solomons Province, Division of Education, 33 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only Uisai-language publications; a primer sometimes carries an alphabet/orthography note, but a stress statement is unlikely.

sources.citation: Hemmilä, Ritva (ed.). 1998. Orthography and phonology database: Islands and Momase Regions. Data Papers on Papua New Guinea Languages 43. Ukarumpa: SIL PNG.

sources.note: Published compendium of SIL PNG OPD sheets; would give the citable published form of the Buin stress statement and show whether any Uisai sheet exists.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1966-67 and 1980s. Buin/Uisai field notes and tape recordings (Paariro; NE dialect forms cited in Laycock 2003), deposited at PARADISEC / ANU.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Laycock is the only linguist known to have recorded Uisai forms; his notebooks might mark accent. catalog.paradisec.org.au is an automated-access block-challenged by automated download; not verified to exist as a Uisai item.

sources.citation: Allen, Jerry & Conrad Hurd. 1965. Languages of the Bougainville District. Ukarumpa: Summer Institute of Linguistics. (pp. 4-7 on Buin dialects incl. Uisai)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The survey that established Uisai as a Buin dialect; would settle the dialect/language identity and may carry a phonological note per dialect.

sources.citation: Cooper, Pam & Margie Griffin. 1965. Buin phonemes. Manuscript, SIL, Ukarumpa (named in the bibliography of Griffin 1996 OPD, per the tere1278 check record).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Underlying SIL phoneme study behind the OPD stress statement; the likeliest place for a fuller treatment of stress in Buin varieties.
